neighbours.label: the head after a colour word when it names a person's body or clothing (-eyed, -skinned, -faced, -shirt), as against coloured objects
fire: The brown-eyed baby smiled at the nurse.
In the tale a blue-skinned giant guards the bridge.
The pale-faced clerk dropped the ledger.
A purple-faced sergeant yelled at the recruits.
The freshman sat out as a redshirt last season.
Fans in green shirts filled the north stand.
The gold-eyed cat belonged to a pink-skinned wizard.
He redshirted as a freshman before starting at guard.
quiet: The brown cart rolled past the nurse.
In the tale a blue bridge crosses the river.
The pale wall behind the clerk was cracked.
A purple flag flew above the recruits.
The freshman sat out with a red card last season.
Fans in the green stand cheered at the north end.
The gold ring was found in a pink box by the wizard.
He blushed at the redshift chart before starting his talk.

notes: Probe: 'green-skinned' 1.06, 'red-faced' 0.87, 'red shirt' 0.61, 'blue door' 0.14, 'black car' 0.07, but hyphenated object compounds leak ('blue-painted' 0.29, '-tinted' 0.27, '-brick' 0.25), so near misses are mostly unhyphenated. The + pole fires on red/green compounds naming things (redshift, red phosphorus, Red Dwarf), which looks like the other side of the distinction.
